risks.title: Loss of exclusivity for key products
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions a loss of exclusivity (LOE) for Atozet and Rosuzet, negatively impacting sales by $197M in 2025. The language emphasizes a major and repeated impact. 'Industrial' category is heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Increased generic competition
risks.score_rationale: Cited for NuvaRing and Singulair, with sales declines of 21% and 30%. The text indicates ongoing pressure, particularly in the United States. Language is concerned and repeated.

risks.title: Pricing pressure in China (VBP)
risks.score_rationale: Volume-Based Procurement (VBP) in China is cited as a future negative factor for the generic drug portfolio. Explicit mention of negative impact over several upcoming quarters.

risks.title: Dependence on acquired commercial rights
risks.score_rationale: The acquisition of Tofidence rights from Biogen involves upfront payments and sales royalties. Risk of uncertainty regarding future profitability and sales-linked payments.

risks.title: Manufacturing network restructuring
risks.score_rationale: Costs related to the optimization of manufacturing and distribution network, with restructuring costs of $95M in 2025. Mention of costly adjustments and inevitable losses on supplier contracts.

risks.title: Discontinuation of R&D programs
risks.score_rationale: Termination of clinical programs for OG-6219 and OG-7191 in 2025. This reduces the future pipeline and weakens long-term growth. Explicitly mentioned in R&D charges.

risks.title: Concentration of commercial risks in the United States
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions pricing pressures, rebates, and customer contracts in the United States, affecting Dulera, NuvaRing, and Singulair. Macro risk related to U.S. healthcare policies.
